title.en: UAE Type Approval Policy Version 4 is now effective

summary.en: TDRA’s unified Type Approval Policy Version 4 became effective on 1 May 2026 and consolidates the main policy, requirements, procedures, testing, customs, market surveillance framework.

body.en:
TDRA states that Version 4 is the updated unified regulatory reference for telecommunications equipment and technologies in the UAE.

The policy consolidates previous Type Approval instruments and applies to relevant activities including registration, approval, import, distribution, display, sale and commercial use. The official policy was issued on 21 January 2026 and became effective on 1 May 2026.

For a specific product, the applicable route, technical evidence, service treatment should be checked against the current TDRA system and policy before filing.

whatKnow.en: Use Version 4 as the primary TDRA reference rather than relying on older Version 3 documents.

sourceName: TDRA — Type Approval Policy Version 4 / Official FAQ

body.en:
Jordan’s Telecommunications Regulatory Commission provides a dedicated Type Approval reference covering the instructions for telecommunications devices, technical rules and standards, annexes and the automated ETAS system.

The TRC service guide describes an online process: create an ETAS account, submit the application, upload the service requirements, complete the application process and receive the official approval letter when the requirements are complete.

Manufacturers should use the current TRC instructions and technical rules when preparing a Jordan submission.

whatKnow.en: Jordan applications are coordinated through the ETAS route, so the technical file should be prepared for online submission and the current TRC requirements.

title.en: Algeria updates electronic communications equipment approval framework

summary.en: ARPCE announced publication of Executive Decree No. 26-97 dated 31 January 2026, establishing conditions and procedures for approval of electronic communications equipment.

body.en:
ARPCE states that Executive Decree No. 26-97 establishes the conditions and procedures for approval of electronic communications equipment.

The framework covers application conditions, processing deadlines, and the issue and validity of the certificate of conformity. ARPCE’s current FAQ states that the response time may not exceed two months from submission of a complete file.

The authority also identifies terminal equipment and radio installations intended for connection to a public electronic communications network among the equipment subject to approval.

whatKnow.en: The 2026 decree should be treated as the current primary approval framework for applicable Algerian equipment.

title.en: Egypt NTRA publishes updated 2026 Type Approval schemes

summary.en: NTRA currently applies Light, Intermediate and Tight Type Approval schemes and provides 2026 procedure documents and a scheme-determination process.

body.en:
NTRA’s current Type Approval procedure page identifies three schemes: Light, Intermediate and Tight.

The authority provides 2026 procedure documents and a scheme determination chart/interactive questions to identify the route applicable to a product. The procedure also includes the associated forms.

Manufacturers should determine the applicable scheme before preparing the final evidence package, because testing and documentation can differ by route.

whatKnow.en: Do not assume one approval route applies to every product. The NTRA scheme must be determined from the product characteristics and applicable country category.

title.en: Bahrain Updates Technical Specifications for Type Approval – Version 1.1

summary.en: Bahrain's Telecommunications Regulatory Authority has released Version 1.1 of its Technical Specifications Requirements for Type Approval, introducing amendments to the technical requirements and specifications applicable to telecommunications and wireless equipment.

body.en:
Bahrain Updates Technical Specifications for Type Approval – Version 1.1

The Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (TRA) of the Kingdom of Bahrain has released Version 1.1 of its Technical Specifications Requirements for Type Approval.

The updated document was released on July 30, 2026, and replaces the first edition published in February 2024. According to the TRA, the revision introduces amendments to the technical requirements and specifications applicable to Type Approval in Bahrain.

What Has Changed?

Version 1.1 establishes the current technical reference for assessing telecommunications and wireless equipment intended for the Bahraini market.

The update affects the technical specifications and requirements used when evaluating equipment for Type Approval. Manufacturers and regulatory teams should therefore review the updated document when preparing new applications or assessing existing compliance documentation.

The TRA has not publicly detailed every individual technical amendment in its announcement. Manufacturers should therefore review the full Version 1.1 document rather than assuming that requirements remain identical to the previous edition.

Products Covered

The Type Approval framework applies to telecommunications and wireless equipment covered by Bahrain's regulatory requirements, including:

Telecommunications equipment

Terminal devices

Short-range wireless devices

RF equipment

Wireless networking equipment

Wi-Fi and Bluetooth-enabled products

IoT and connected devices

Other radio and telecommunications equipment subject to Type Approval

What Manufacturers Need to Know

Manufacturers and exporters planning to introduce telecommunications or wireless equipment into Bahrain should review Version 1.1 before submitting new Type Approval applications.

Companies should:

Review the current technical specifications applicable to their product.

Check whether existing test reports continue to correspond to the applicable requirements.

Review RF, EMC and safety documentation where applicable.

Ensure that technical specifications and product configurations are consistent with the submitted documentation.

Update compliance references that rely on the superseded 2024 edition.

Assess existing approved products when preparing renewals, modifications or new product variants.

Bahrain Type Approval Process

The TRA requires telecommunications equipment imported into Bahrain to obtain Type Approval before being made available on the local market.

Applications are submitted through the TRA's eTRA portal. The published requirements include a Declaration of Conformity, technical datasheet and, where applicable, EMC, safety and radio test reports, together with other supporting technical documentation.

The TRA also requires applicants for Type Approval to be locally commercially registered companies or to follow the applicable local representative requirements.

Market Access Considerations

For international manufacturers, the release of Version 1.1 means that compliance assessments for the Bahraini market should be based on the current technical specifications.

Manufacturers should review their technical files before shipment and confirm that the applicable standards, test reports and product specifications remain aligned with Bahrain's current regulatory requirements.

AFAQ JOOD supports international manufacturers, exporters and technology companies with Type Approval and regulatory compliance coordination across selected markets in the Middle East and Africa.

Our team assists clients in identifying applicable requirements, organizing technical documentation and coordinating regulatory procedures with relevant authorities and local stakeholders.

Manufacturers planning to introduce telecommunications, wireless, RF or ICT equipment into Bahrain should assess the applicable Type Approval requirements before market entry.

Regulatory requirements may vary according to the product category, technology and applicable technical specifications. Manufacturers should verify the requirements applicable to their specific equipment before submitting an application or shipping products to Bahrain.

whatKnow.en:
Manufacturers and exporters supplying telecommunications and wireless equipment to Bahrain should review Version 1.1 of the Type Approval Technical Specifications and verify that their products, technical documentation and applicable test reports remain aligned with the current requirements.

Companies preparing new Type Approval applications should use Version 1.1 as the current technical reference and review any existing compliance documentation that refers to the previous edition.

title.en: Oman Introduces Self-Declaration of Conformity for Selected Telecom Devices

summary.en: Oman's Telecommunications Regulatory Authority has introduced a Self-Declaration of Conformity service within its Type Approval system for selected categories of telecommunications and ICT devices.

body.en:
Oman Introduces Self-Declaration of Conformity for Selected Telecom Devices

Oman's Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (TRA) has introduced a Self-Declaration of Conformity route within its Type Approval framework for selected telecommunications and ICT products.

The new route provides eligible applicants with an alternative compliance procedure based on a declaration confirming that the equipment meets the applicable technical and regulatory requirements.

What Manufacturers Need to Know

The Self-Declaration route is not applicable to all telecommunications equipment. It is intended for specific product categories, and manufacturers should confirm their product's eligibility before selecting this pathway.

Products identified as eligible include certain:

Wireless keyboards and mice
Printers
Speakers
Smart pens
Wireless chargers
Unmanaged switches
Smart watches
Hearing-assistance devices
Projectors

Manufacturers should ensure that the product complies with the applicable technical requirements and that the information provided in the Declaration of Conformity is accurate and supported by appropriate technical documentation.

Type Approval in Oman

Oman's TRA operates an electronic Type Approval system for telecommunications and ICT equipment.

The Authority's published requirements include a Declaration of Conformity, equipment technical specifications and, where applicable, RF, EMC and safety test reports from appropriately accredited laboratories.

The Type Approval system also supports related regulatory procedures, including import authorization and customs release.

What This Means for Manufacturers

For international manufacturers preparing to enter the Omani market, the introduction of a Self-Declaration route for selected products provides an additional compliance pathway.

However, manufacturers should not assume that a product qualifies automatically. Eligibility depends on the product category and the applicable regulatory requirements.

Before shipment, manufacturers should:

Identify the applicable Type Approval pathway.
Confirm whether the product is eligible for Self-Declaration.
Review the applicable technical requirements.
Prepare the required Declaration of Conformity and supporting documentation.
Verify that the product configuration matches the submitted documentation.
Confirm any applicable import and market-access requirements.

Early regulatory assessment can help manufacturers identify the correct approval pathway and avoid unnecessary delays during market entry.

AFAQ JOOD Regulatory Support

AFAQ JOOD supports international manufacturers, exporters and technology companies with Type Approval and regulatory compliance coordination across selected markets in the Middle East and Africa.

Our team assists clients in identifying applicable regulatory requirements, organizing technical documentation and coordinating approval procedures with relevant authorities and local stakeholders.

Manufacturers planning to introduce wireless, telecommunications or ICT products into Oman can contact AFAQ JOOD for regulatory coordination and market-access support.

whatKnow.en: Manufacturers of eligible products can use the Self-Declaration of Conformity service as part of Oman's Type Approval process. The option is limited to specific product categories, so manufacturers should confirm eligibility before relying on the self-declaration route.

title.en: Kuwait Opens Compliance Window for Unlicensed Wireless Devices

summary.en: Kuwait's Communications and Information Technology Regulatory Authority (CITRA) has opened a three-month compliance window for unlicensed wireless devices circulating in the country, allowing concerned parties to regularize their status without penalties during the announced period

body.en:
Kuwait's Communications and Information Technology Regulatory Authority (CITRA) has announced a three-month compliance window for unlicensed wireless devices currently circulating in the country.

The announcement, issued on June 8, 2026, provides an opportunity for concerned parties to regularize the status of unlicensed wireless equipment during the specified period without penalties when the equipment is surrendered within the announced timeframe.

### Why This Matters for Manufacturers and Suppliers

The announcement highlights the importance of ensuring that wireless and telecommunications equipment entering the Kuwaiti market complies with the country's regulatory framework.

Manufacturers, suppliers and importers should assess the regulatory status of their products before shipment and confirm whether the equipment requires Type Approval or another authorization from CITRA.

### Products That May Be Affected

The regulatory requirements may be relevant to a wide range of wireless and telecommunications products, including:

* Wireless communication equipment
* Wi-Fi and networking equipment
* RF equipment
* Radio communication devices
* Wireless IoT products
* Short-range wireless devices
* Telecommunications terminal equipment
* Other equipment operating through regulated wireless technologies

The specific requirements depend on the product type, technical characteristics, wireless technologies and applicable regulatory requirements.

### Type Approval Requirements in Kuwait

CITRA provides a Type Approval service for telecommunications devices to ensure their compatibility with approved technical specifications.

The authority's published requirements include technical specifications of the equipment, authorization from the manufacturer, applicable Declaration of Conformity documentation and laboratory reports from approved laboratories.

CITRA's Type Approval regulations also cover wired and wireless communication devices and establish procedures for reviewing technical documentation and verifying testing conducted by recognized and accredited laboratories.

### What Manufacturers Should Consider

Manufacturers and exporters planning to enter the Kuwaiti market should:

* Identify the applicable CITRA requirements before shipment.
* Determine whether Type Approval is required for the product.
* Verify the technical specifications and applicable standards.
* Prepare the required Declaration of Conformity and supporting documents.
* Ensure that laboratory test reports meet the applicable requirements.
* Confirm that the product configuration matches the submitted technical documentation.
* Coordinate the regulatory process before importing or commercializing the equipment.

Early regulatory assessment can help companies identify compliance requirements and reduce potential delays during the market-entry process.

### AFAQ JOOD Regulatory Support

AFAQ JOOD supports international manufacturers, exporters and technology companies with Type Approval and regulatory compliance coordination across selected markets in the Middle East and Africa.

Our team assists clients in understanding applicable requirements, organizing technical documentation and coordinating regulatory procedures with relevant authorities and local stakeholders.

Manufacturers planning to introduce wireless or telecommunications equipment into Kuwait should assess the applicable regulatory pathway before shipment to help ensure a structured market-entry process.

Regulatory requirements may vary according to the product category, technology and intended use. Manufacturers should verify the requirements applicable to their specific equipment before entering the Kuwaiti market.

whatKnow.en:
Manufacturers, suppliers and importers of wireless equipment intended for the Kuwaiti market should verify that their products comply with the applicable CITRA requirements before importation, distribution or use.

Companies should confirm whether their equipment requires Type Approval or other regulatory authorization and ensure that the relevant technical documentation, conformity information and laboratory reports are available where required.

CITRA's current Type Approval service covers telecommunications devices and requires technical specifications, manufacturer authorization, applicable Declaration of Conformity documentation and laboratory reports from approved laboratories

title.en: Qatar Updates Its National Frequency Allocation Plan for Wireless and Radio Equipment

summary.en: Qatar's Communications Regulatory Authority has issued an updated National Frequency Allocation Plan, reflecting developments in radio spectrum use and supporting the country's growing demand for wireless communications and emerging technologies

body.en:
Qatar's Communications Regulatory Authority (CRA) has issued an updated version of the Qatar National Frequency Allocation Plan, reflecting the continued development of wireless communications and the increasing demand for radio-frequency spectrum in the country.

The updated plan provides an important regulatory reference for the use of radio frequencies across different services and technologies and supports the efficient management of spectrum resources in Qatar.

### What Does the Update Mean?

The National Frequency Allocation Plan establishes the framework for how radio-frequency spectrum is allocated to different services and applications.

For manufacturers and technology companies, the frequency allocation framework is particularly relevant when developing or exporting products that incorporate radio or wireless technologies.

Products operating within regulated frequency bands may need to comply with applicable technical and regulatory requirements before they can be imported, used or commercialized in Qatar.

### Products That May Be Affected

The update is relevant to a wide range of wireless and radio-enabled products, including:

* Wireless networking equipment
* Wi-Fi-enabled devices
* RF equipment
* Cellular and mobile equipment
* Internet of Things (IoT) devices
* Short-range wireless devices
* Wireless cameras
* Radio communication equipment
* Satellite communication equipment
* Other telecommunications equipment using regulated radio frequencies

The specific requirements applicable to a product depend on its technology, operating frequencies, intended use and applicable regulatory framework.

### What Manufacturers Should Consider

Manufacturers planning to enter the Qatari market should assess the regulatory requirements applicable to their products before shipment.

Key considerations include:

* Identifying the radio frequencies used by the equipment.
* Confirming that the operating frequencies are permitted for the intended application.
* Reviewing applicable technical and regulatory requirements.
* Preparing relevant technical documentation and test reports.
* Determining whether Type Approval is required.
* Checking applicable import and market-access procedures.
* Ensuring that the product configuration and technical specifications are consistent with the submitted documentation.

Qatar's CRA provides Type Approval procedures for Radio and Telecommunications Terminal Equipment (RTTE) through its e-Spectrum services platform. The platform allows applicants to submit and track Type Approval applications for applicable equipment.

### Regulatory Compliance in Qatar

The updated National Frequency Allocation Plan represents an important reference for companies developing or supplying wireless technologies in Qatar.

Manufacturers should consider regulatory assessment at an early stage of the product launch process to identify applicable frequency, Type Approval and market-access requirements.

Requirements may vary according to the product category, technology, frequency bands and intended application. Manufacturers should therefore verify the requirements applicable to their specific equipment before entering the Qatari market.

### AFAQ JOOD Regulatory Support

AFAQ JOOD supports international manufacturers, exporters and technology companies with Type Approval and regulatory compliance coordination across selected markets in the Middle East and Africa.

Our team helps clients assess applicable requirements, organize technical documentation and coordinate regulatory procedures with relevant authorities and local stakeholders.

For manufacturers planning to introduce wireless or telecommunications equipment into Qatar, early regulatory assessment can help establish a clear and structured market-entry pathway.

whatKnow.en:
Manufacturers of wireless and radio-enabled products should review the applicable frequency and regulatory requirements before introducing their products into the Qatari market.

The updated frequency allocation framework is particularly relevant to products that operate on regulated radio frequencies. Manufacturers should verify the applicable frequency bands, technical requirements and regulatory procedures for their specific equipment.

For telecommunications and radio terminal equipment, Qatar's Communications Regulatory Authority provides regulatory procedures for Type Approval through its e-Spectrum platform. Manufacturers and importers should ensure that the required technical documentation and conformity information are prepared before market entry

title.en: Saudi Arabia Updates Wireless Regulatory Requirements for ICT Equipment

summary.en: Saudi Arabia has introduced important regulatory changes affecting wireless ICT equipment, with updated conformity and market-access requirements for manufacturers and importers of connected and radio-enabled devices

body.en:
Saudi Arabia has introduced important regulatory changes affecting wireless Information and Communication Technology (ICT) equipment, reinforcing the requirements that manufacturers and importers need to consider when placing connected and radio-enabled products on the Saudi market.

The regulatory framework involves both the Communications, Space & Technology Commission (CST) and the Saudi Standards, Metrology and Quality Organization (SASO), with requirements applying according to the type and characteristics of the equipment.

### What Products May Be Affected?

The requirements are particularly relevant to products that incorporate wireless or radio functionality, including:

* Wireless networking equipment and routers
* Cellular and mobile devices
* Internet of Things (IoT) equipment
* Short-range wireless devices
* Radio-frequency (RF) equipment
* Connected ICT products
* Other devices operating through regulated radio technologies

Manufacturers should identify the applicable technical and conformity requirements before shipping products to Saudi Arabia.

### Regulatory Compliance and Market Access

For international manufacturers, understanding the relationship between technical regulations, conformity assessment, product certification and telecommunications requirements is an important part of the Saudi market-entry process.

Depending on the product category, manufacturers may need to complete applicable conformity procedures and ensure that the equipment meets the relevant Saudi technical requirements before importation and commercialization.

The CST continues to play a central role in regulating telecommunications and ICT equipment, including requirements related to telecommunications devices, radio equipment and spectrum use.

### What Manufacturers Should Consider

Companies planning to introduce wireless products into Saudi Arabia should review their products before shipment and determine:

* The applicable Saudi technical requirements
* Whether the product falls within telecommunications or radio equipment regulations
* Applicable conformity assessment requirements
* Required technical documentation and test reports
* Radio-frequency and spectrum-related requirements, where applicable
* Import and market-access requirements

Early regulatory assessment can help manufacturers avoid unnecessary delays during the approval and import process.

### AFAQ JOOD Regulatory Support

AFAQ JOOD supports international manufacturers, exporters and technology companies with Type Approval and regulatory compliance coordination across selected markets in the Middle East and Africa.

Our team helps clients understand applicable requirements, organize technical documentation and coordinate regulatory procedures with the relevant authorities and local stakeholders.

For companies planning to enter the Saudi Arabian market, obtaining a clear understanding of the applicable regulatory pathway at an early stage can help make the market-access process more structured and efficient.

**Regulatory requirements may vary depending on the product type, technology, frequency bands and applicable Saudi regulations. Manufacturers should verify the requirements applicable to their specific product before market entry.**

whatKnow.en:
Manufacturers planning to introduce wireless and ICT equipment into the Saudi Arabian market should assess the applicable regulatory requirements before shipment.

The requirements may vary depending on the product category, wireless technologies, frequency bands, intended use and applicable Saudi technical regulations. Manufacturers should therefore:

* Identify the applicable regulatory and technical requirements for the product.
* Confirm whether the equipment falls under telecommunications, radio or other regulated product categories.
* Prepare the required technical documentation and relevant test reports.

Early regulatory assessment can help manufacturers identify potential compliance issues and reduce delays during the market-entry process.

title.en: Yemen Updates Requirements for Telecommunications Equipment Import and Type Approval

summary.en: Yemen's Ministry of Telecommunications and Information Technology has published requirements for the Type Approval and importation of telecommunications equipment, including technical documentation, conformity declarations and supporting test reports.

body.en:
Yemen Updates Requirements for Telecommunications Equipment Import and Type Approval

Yemen's Ministry of Telecommunications and Information Technology has published requirements governing the Type Approval and importation of telecommunications equipment.

The requirements are intended to ensure that telecommunications equipment entering the market meets the applicable technical and regulatory conditions before importation and use.

Type Approval Requirements

The Type Approval process requires manufacturers and applicants to provide technical information and supporting documentation for the equipment.

The published requirements include a description of the equipment, technical specifications, product catalogues, a manufacturer's Declaration of Conformity, relevant test reports, laboratory information, user documentation and product photographs.

The documentation allows the relevant authority to assess the equipment against the applicable technical requirements.

Products That May Require Approval

The requirements may apply to a wide range of telecommunications and wireless products, including:

Wireless communication equipment

RF equipment

Wi-Fi and Bluetooth devices

Cellular and mobile equipment

IoT devices

Networking equipment

Satellite communication equipment

Radio communication equipment

Other telecommunications and ICT equipment subject to applicable requirements

What Manufacturers Need to Know

Manufacturers and exporters planning to supply telecommunications equipment to Yemen should determine the applicable regulatory requirements before shipment.

Technical documentation should accurately identify the product model, manufacturer, technical characteristics and intended operation.

Manufacturers should also ensure that supporting test reports and conformity documentation correspond to the exact product model being submitted.

Inconsistent information between the product, technical documentation and test reports can create additional regulatory review requirements and may delay the approval process.

Import Authorization

The Type Approval process is an important part of the regulatory pathway for telecommunications equipment entering the market.

The Ministry's published guidance indicates that equipment should not be imported before the required approvals and authorizations have been obtained.

Manufacturers and importers should therefore complete the applicable regulatory procedures before shipment and coordinate the required documentation with the local applicant or representative.

Preparing for Type Approval

Before submitting an application, manufacturers should prepare a complete technical file containing the applicable specifications, conformity documentation, test reports and product information.

A structured documentation package can help facilitate the regulatory review and reduce the possibility of requests for additional information.

AFAQ JOOD Regulatory Support

AFAQ JOOD supports international manufacturers, exporters and technology companies with Type Approval and regulatory compliance coordination across selected markets in the Middle East and Africa.

Our team assists clients in identifying applicable requirements, organizing technical documentation and coordinating regulatory procedures with relevant authorities and local stakeholders.

Manufacturers planning to introduce telecommunications, wireless, RF or ICT equipment into Yemen should assess the applicable regulatory pathway before shipment.

Regulatory requirements may vary according to the product category, technology and destination. Manufacturers should verify the requirements applicable to their specific equipment before entering the Yemeni market.

whatKnow.en:
Manufacturers and exporters planning to introduce telecommunications equipment into Yemen should review the applicable Type Approval and import requirements before shipment.

Applicants may need to provide technical specifications, product catalogues, a manufacturer's Declaration of Conformity, relevant test reports, laboratory information, user documentation and product photographs.

Manufacturers should ensure that the model number, technical specifications and supporting documents are consistent throughout the application package.

title.en: Yemen’s Aden Authority Establishes a Separate Type Approval Pathway

summary.en: Yemen's telecommunications regulatory framework now includes a separate Type Approval pathway administered from Aden for telecommunications and wireless equipment intended for Aden-controlled areas.

body.en:
Yemen’s Aden Authority Establishes a Separate Type Approval Pathway

Yemen’s telecommunications regulatory framework has developed a separate Type Approval pathway administered from Aden for telecommunications and wireless equipment intended for areas under the Aden-based authority’s administration.

The development creates a distinct regulatory route for manufacturers and importers supplying telecommunications equipment through southern entry points and into Aden-administered areas.

A Separate Certification Pathway

The Type Approval framework in Yemen is currently administered through separate authorities based in Sana’a and Aden.

The Aden-based Ministry of Telecommunications and Information Technology provides services for telecommunications equipment, including import permits and Type Approval applications.

The Ministry’s electronic services platform identifies Type Approval and import authorization services for telecommunications equipment and provides information for companies seeking regulatory approval.

Products That May Be Affected

The regulatory process may apply to a broad range of telecommunications and wireless products, including:

Wireless communication equipment

RF equipment

Wi-Fi and Bluetooth devices

Cellular and mobile equipment

IoT devices

Networking equipment

Satellite communication equipment

Radio communication equipment

Other telecommunications and ICT equipment subject to applicable requirements

What Manufacturers Need to Know

Manufacturers and exporters planning to supply products to Aden-administered areas should determine the applicable regulatory pathway before shipment.

The destination and distribution plan should be established at the beginning of the compliance process, as Type Approval issued through the Sana’a and Aden authorities should not be assumed to be mutually recognized.

Applicants should prepare the technical documentation required for the applicable authority, including product specifications, technical catalogues, manufacturer's Declaration of Conformity, relevant test reports and other supporting documents.

Market Access Considerations

The development of a separate Aden Type Approval pathway is particularly relevant to international manufacturers whose products enter Yemen through southern ports or are intended for distribution in Aden-administered areas.

Companies with products intended for multiple regions of Yemen should assess the regulatory requirements for each destination before shipment.

Manufacturers should also consider the applicable customs and import procedures and coordinate their documentation with the local importer or representative.

Preparing for Type Approval

Before submitting an application, manufacturers should ensure that the product model, technical specifications, test reports and conformity documentation are consistent.

A complete technical file can help reduce additional information requests during regulatory review and facilitate the market-entry process.

AFAQ JOOD Regulatory Support

AFAQ JOOD supports international manufacturers, exporters and technology companies with Type Approval and regulatory compliance coordination across selected markets in the Middle East and Africa.

For products intended for Yemen, our team can assist manufacturers in identifying the applicable regulatory pathway, preparing technical documentation and coordinating the approval process with relevant local stakeholders.

Manufacturers planning to supply telecommunications, wireless, RF or ICT equipment to Aden-administered areas should assess the applicable Type Approval requirements before shipment.

Regulatory requirements may vary according to the product category, technology and destination. Manufacturers should verify the applicable requirements for their specific equipment before entering the Yemeni market.

whatKnow.en: Manufacturers and exporters planning to supply telecommunications equipment to Aden-controlled areas should assess the Aden Type Approval pathway separately from the Sana’a process. Companies should determine the intended destination of their products before selecting the applicable certification route and prepare the technical documentation required by the relevant authority

title.en: Lebanon TRA Clarifies Manufacturer-Based Type Approval Certificates

summary.en: Lebanon’s Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (TRA) has issued a clarification on the Type Approval procedure for telecom-enabled equipment, addressing the relationship between manufacturers, approved models, and importers.

body.en:
Lebanon TRA Clarifies Manufacturer-Based Type Approval Certificates

Lebanon’s Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (TRA) has issued a clarification concerning the Type Approval procedure for equipment with telecommunications capabilities.

On September 2, 2026, the TRA issued Notification No. TRA/PRE/327-020926, addressing the relationship between Type Approval applications, manufacturers, approved models, and the importation of identical products into Lebanon.

According to the notification, as reported by specialist regulatory compliance sources, a Type Approval application may be submitted in the name of the manufacturer, either directly by the manufacturer or through an authorized representative.

The corresponding Type Approval Certificate is issued in the manufacturer’s name for the specific approved model or product. The notification states that importers bringing the identical approved product into Lebanon may rely on the manufacturer-based Type Approval, provided that the imported equipment corresponds to the approved model and technical specifications covered by the valid certificate.

What Manufacturers Need to Know

Manufacturers supplying telecommunications and radio-enabled products to Lebanon should ensure that the product model, technical specifications, telecommunications functions, and supporting documentation submitted for Type Approval accurately correspond to the products intended for importation.

The clarification is particularly relevant to international manufacturers whose products may be supplied to the Lebanese market through multiple importers or distributors.

Manufacturers may submit applications directly or through an authorized representative, depending on the applicable procedure and representation arrangements.

Affected Products

The clarification is relevant to telecommunications-enabled products, including:

Telecommunications equipment

Radio and wireless equipment

RF equipment

Wi-Fi and Bluetooth devices

Cellular and mobile equipment

IoT and connected devices

Telecommunications modules

Embedded telecommunications equipment

Radio components

Telecommunications terminal equipment

Other products subject to Lebanon Type Approval requirements

Technical Compliance

The TRA Type Approval framework requires applicants to provide appropriate technical documentation and evidence of compliance.

Depending on the equipment, the Technical Compliance Folder may include technical data sheets, user manuals, product specifications, drawings and schematics, antenna information for wireless equipment, product photographs, applicable technical standards, and third-party test reports.

The TRA states that recognized laboratory test results should come from laboratories accredited according to ISO/IEC 17025 through an appropriate accreditation body or an ILAC member.

Applicants are also required to prepare a Declaration of Conformity with the applicable specifications.

Regulatory Framework

The issuance of Type Approval certificates is currently handled by Lebanon’s Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (TRA). The TRA also maintains the current Type Approval Regulation, application procedures, forms, and technical requirements on its official website.

The TRA’s current regulatory framework was updated following the transfer of Type Approval certification responsibilities from the Ministry of Telecommunications to the TRA in accordance with the applicable regulatory decisions.

Important Regulatory Note

The September 2, 2026 notification has been reported by specialist regulatory compliance sources as clarifying the use of manufacturer-based Type Approval for identical products.

However, manufacturers and importers should verify the applicable procedure directly with the TRA before relying on the clarification for a specific shipment, as the TRA’s currently published FAQ pages contain additional provisions concerning importer-specific Type Approval certificates and importation procedures.

Companies should therefore confirm the applicable certificate structure and documentation requirements with the TRA for each product and import scenario.

What This Means for Manufacturers

International manufacturers planning to enter the Lebanese market should review their Type Approval strategy before shipping products.

Particular attention should be given to:

Manufacturer and authorized representative information

Exact product and model identification

Technical specifications

Radio and telecommunications functions

Test reports

Declaration of Conformity

Technical Compliance Folder

Applicable Type Approval classification

Importation and customs requirements

TRA labeling requirements

AFAQ JOOD Regulatory Support

AFAQ JOOD supports manufacturers, OEMs, ODMs, exporters, distributors, and technology companies with Type Approval and regulatory coordination across Middle East and African markets.

Our team can assist with regulatory assessment, technical documentation, manufacturer authorization, application preparation, Type Approval coordination, and regulatory follow-up for telecommunications, RF, wireless, IoT, and other regulated technology products entering the Lebanese market.

whatKnow.en:
The Lebanese Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (TRA) issued Notification No. TRA/PRE/327-020926 on September 2, 2026, clarifying the Type Approval procedure for equipment with telecommunications capabilities.

According to the notification as reported by specialist regulatory compliance sources, the Type Approval application may be submitted in the name of the manufacturer, either directly by the manufacturer or through an authorized representative.

The resulting Type Approval Certificate is issued in the manufacturer’s name for the specific approved model or product. The notification states that importers bringing the identical approved product into Lebanon may rely on the manufacturer-based Type Approval, provided that the imported equipment corresponds to the approved model and technical specifications.

Manufacturers should therefore ensure that the model number, product specifications, telecommunications functions, and technical documentation submitted for Type Approval accurately correspond to the products intended for the Lebanese market.

title.en: Nigeria NCC Strengthens Type Approval Compliance for SIM-Enabled Devices

summary.en: Nigeria’s Communications Commission (NCC) is strengthening Type Approval compliance for SIM-enabled communication devices through a technology-based compliance framework supported by a Device Management System (DMS).

body.en:
Nigeria NCC Strengthens Type Approval Compliance for SIM-Enabled Devices

Nigeria’s Communications Commission (NCC) is strengthening Type Approval compliance for communication devices through a technology-based regulatory framework designed to improve the identification and verification of compliant equipment.

The initiative focuses particularly on communication devices equipped with SIM functionality and introduces a Device Management System (DMS) as a technological platform supporting automated Type Approval compliance monitoring.

According to the NCC, the framework is intended to make Type Approval compliance more efficient and consistent while strengthening oversight of communication devices entering, being sold, and operating in Nigeria.

Type Approval Requirement

Under Section 132(2) of the Nigerian Communications Act 2003, communication equipment covered by the applicable requirements must obtain Type Approval from the NCC before being sold or used in Nigeria.

The new compliance framework strengthens the Commission’s ability to verify whether devices entering the Nigerian market have satisfied the applicable Type Approval requirements.

Device Management System

The Device Management System (DMS) will support the automated verification of communication devices and their Type Approval status.

The NCC has stated that the implementation is being carried out in cooperation with key stakeholders, including the Nigeria Customs Service, Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs), importers, and relevant market associations.

The initial implementation focuses on incorporating devices already in the market and ensuring that future imported devices are appropriately registered and authenticated.

Central Equipment Identity Register

The NCC has linked the implementation of the new compliance framework to the Central Equipment Identity Register (CEIR), established under the Type Approval Business Rules issued in August 2024.

The CEIR maintains records associated with communication devices operating in Nigeria, including International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI) information for applicable devices.

According to the NCC, the centralized system is intended to strengthen the Commission’s ability to identify devices that do not comply with applicable regulatory requirements.

Impact on SIM-Enabled Devices

The NCC has stated that SIM-enabled communication devices entering Nigeria will be subject to the applicable registration and authentication requirements.

Devices that have not been properly registered and authenticated may be prevented from operating on Nigerian mobile networks under the applicable framework.

The system is also intended to help identify illegally imported or non-compliant devices and support the identification of devices reported as stolen.

Affected Products

The development is particularly relevant to:

Mobile phones

SIM-enabled communication devices

Cellular equipment

IoT devices with cellular connectivity

Wireless communication equipment

Telecommunications terminal equipment

Connected devices containing IMEI identifiers

Other communication equipment subject to NCC Type Approval requirements

What Manufacturers and Importers Need to Know

Manufacturers, OEMs, exporters, and importers supplying communication equipment to Nigeria should ensure that applicable Type Approval requirements are completed before products are introduced into the Nigerian market.

Companies should maintain consistency between the products submitted for Type Approval and the equipment subsequently imported and distributed in Nigeria.

Particular attention should be given to:

Product model identification

IMEI and device identity information where applicable

Technical specifications

Test reports

Declaration of Conformity

Technical construction documentation

Product and equipment labeling

Type Approval certification

Applicable registration and authentication requirements

Manufacturers should also monitor the implementation of the DMS and CEIR framework as the NCC continues to strengthen automated compliance verification.

Regulatory Framework

The NCC currently publishes the Type Approval Regulations 2024 and Type Approval Business Rules 2024 as part of its regulatory framework for telecommunications equipment.

The Commission maintains a list of approved telecommunications equipment and continues to update its regulatory and Type Approval resources.

AFAQ JOOD Regulatory Support

AFAQ JOOD supports manufacturers, OEMs, ODMs, exporters, distributors, and technology companies with Type Approval and regulatory coordination across Middle East and African markets.

Our team can assist with regulatory assessment, technical documentation, manufacturer authorization, application preparation, Type Approval coordination, and regulatory follow-up for telecommunications, RF, wireless, IoT, cellular, and other regulated technology products entering the Nigerian market.

whatKnow.en:
The Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) is strengthening enforcement of Type Approval requirements for communication devices imported, sold, and used in Nigeria.

The new technology-based compliance framework is supported by a Device Management System (DMS), which enables the NCC to electronically verify Type Approval compliance for SIM-enabled devices.

The initiative is being implemented in cooperation with key stakeholders, including the Nigeria Customs Service, original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), importers, and relevant market associations.

Manufacturers and importers should ensure that communication devices entering the Nigerian market have the required Type Approval and are properly registered within the applicable regulatory framework.

title.en: Kenya Opens Consultation on New Technical Specifications for Network Equipment

summary.en: Kenya’s Communications Authority has opened a public consultation on proposed Technical Specifications for Network Equipment, 2026, which will guide the Type Approval of network equipment sold and used in Kenya.

body.en:
Kenya Opens Consultation on New Technical Specifications for Network Equipment

Kenya’s Communications Authority (CA) has opened a public consultation on proposed Technical Specifications for Network Equipment, 2026.

The proposed specifications are intended to guide the Type Approval process for network equipment sold and used in Kenya. The Authority has invited members of the public and stakeholders in the ICT sector to review the proposed requirements and submit their representations by September 30, 2026.

The consultation represents an important regulatory development for manufacturers, vendors, importers, distributors, and technology companies supplying network infrastructure and communications equipment to the Kenyan market.

What Manufacturers Need to Know

The Communications Authority is responsible for the Type Approval and acceptance of telecommunications and radio communication equipment intended for use in Kenya.

Under the proposed 2026 specifications, network equipment will be assessed against the applicable technical requirements before being introduced into the Kenyan market.

Manufacturers and suppliers should review the proposed specifications and evaluate whether their products and existing technical documentation remain aligned with the requirements that may apply following the regulatory process.

Affected Products

The proposed framework is particularly relevant to:

Routers

Network switches

Enterprise networking equipment

Wireless networking equipment

Data communication equipment

Telecommunications network equipment

Network infrastructure equipment

RF and wireless network devices

Other communications equipment subject to Kenya Type Approval requirements

Type Approval in Kenya

The Communications Authority requires communications equipment intended to operate within public telecommunications networks in Kenya to undergo Type Approval or Type Acceptance, as applicable.

The Authority's Type Approval framework covers a wide range of equipment, including mobile cellular devices, radio communication equipment, routers, modems, switches, satellite equipment, and other telecommunications products.

Type Approval is generally carried out for each equipment model, while changes to the model, design, or specifications may require the equipment to be submitted again for approval.

Technical Compliance

The CA evaluates Type Approval applications using technical documentation and conformity evidence.

Depending on the equipment category, manufacturers and applicants may be required to provide technical manuals, user manuals, conformity certificates, and applicable RF, EMC, and safety test reports.

Manufacturers should ensure that the documentation submitted for Type Approval accurately represents the commercial version of the equipment intended for the Kenyan market.

Public Consultation

The Communications Authority has invited ICT industry stakeholders and members of the public to provide comments on the proposed Technical Specifications for Network Equipment, 2026.

Submissions are being accepted until September 30, 2026.

The consultation is intended to provide stakeholders with an opportunity to review the proposed technical framework and provide feedback before the regulatory requirements are finalized.

What This Means for Manufacturers

Companies planning to introduce network equipment into Kenya should monitor the outcome of the consultation and review the proposed technical specifications.

Manufacturers should pay particular attention to:

Product model identification

Technical specifications

RF characteristics where applicable

EMC compliance

Safety requirements

Network interoperability

Technical manuals

Test reports

Declarations and conformity documentation

Type Approval documentation

Manufacturers with products already being prepared for the Kenyan market should also monitor any changes resulting from the consultation before finalizing future compliance submissions.

AFAQ JOOD supports manufacturers, OEMs, ODMs, exporters, distributors, and technology companies with Type Approval and regulatory coordination across Middle East and African markets.

Our team can assist with regulatory assessment, technical documentation, manufacturer authorization, application preparation, Type Approval coordination, and regulatory follow-up for telecommunications, RF, wireless, IoT, networking, and other regulated technology products entering the Kenyan market.

whatKnow.en:
Kenya’s Communications Authority (CA) has developed proposed Technical Specifications for Network Equipment, 2026, to guide the Type Approval process for network equipment sold and used in Kenya.

The Authority has invited members of the public and ICT sector stakeholders to submit comments on the proposed specifications by September 30, 2026.

Manufacturers, vendors, importers, distributors, and other stakeholders supplying network equipment to Kenya should review the proposed technical requirements and assess their potential impact on existing and future Type Approval applications.

title.en: South Africa ICASA Reinforces Equipment Type Approval Requirements

summary.en: South Africa’s ICASA maintains strict Equipment Type Approval requirements for telecommunications and radio equipment, with compliance covering applicable technical standards, RF, EMC, safety, documentation, and local applicant requirements.

body.en:
South Africa ICASA Reinforces Equipment Type Approval Requirements

South Africa’s Independent Communications Authority of South Africa (ICASA) maintains a comprehensive Equipment Type Approval framework for telecommunications and radio equipment used, supplied, sold, or imported into the country.

Under South Africa’s regulatory framework, electronic communications equipment and radio apparatus intended for use in connection with electronic communications must obtain Type Approval from ICASA unless the equipment is specifically exempted.

The framework is designed to ensure that equipment placed on the South African market complies with the applicable technical standards and regulatory requirements.

What Manufacturers Need to Know

Manufacturers, importers, distributors, and technology companies supplying telecommunications equipment to South Africa should ensure that their products meet the applicable ICASA requirements before the equipment is imported, supplied, or offered for sale.

ICASA states that Type Approval applications can be submitted by manufacturers, importers, distributors, or South African registered companies. However, the Type Approval Certificate is issued to a South African registered company.

This makes the local applicant structure an important consideration for international manufacturers entering the South African market.

Technical Compliance Requirements

The ICASA Type Approval process involves assessment of the equipment against the applicable technical standards.

Depending on the equipment category, the compliance process may involve:

Performance testing

Radio frequency testing

Electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) testing

Safety testing

Technical documentation

Product photographs

User manuals

Functional descriptions

Schematic diagrams

PCB information where applicable

Conformity test reports from recognized laboratories

Manufacturers should ensure that submitted test reports correspond exactly to the equipment and model submitted for approval.

Applicable Equipment

The ICASA framework is relevant to a broad range of products, including:

RF equipment

Radio equipment

Mobile phones

Routers

Modems

Wi-Fi equipment

Bluetooth devices

Wireless communication equipment

IoT devices

Two-way radios

Telecommunications terminal equipment

Satellite and wireless communication equipment

Other electronic communications equipment subject to ICASA requirements

Standard and Simplified Type Approval

ICASA provides both Standard and Simplified Type Approval procedures.

Equipment that has not previously received Type Approval generally follows the Standard Type Approval process.

Where equipment is already listed on the ICASA Type Approval Register and the equipment being submitted is identical to the previously approved equipment, the Simplified Type Approval process may apply.

The simplified route can reduce the documentation required during the application, although ICASA may request a representative sample when necessary.

Type Approval Validity

ICASA states that Type Approvals are generally valid for an unlimited period provided that the approved equipment is not modified and that applicable technical standards have not changed in a way that invalidates the approval.

Manufacturers should therefore monitor both product changes and regulatory standard updates after approval.

Type Approval Database

ICASA maintains a database of Type Approved equipment.

Manufacturers and importers can use the database to verify whether equipment has previously been approved and determine whether a Simplified Type Approval route may be applicable.

Labelling Requirements

Approved equipment is subject to ICASA labelling requirements.

Manufacturers and suppliers should ensure that the applicable ICASA identification and labelling requirements are followed for approved equipment and its packaging.

Importance for International Manufacturers

International manufacturers planning to enter the South African market should consider the local applicant requirement at an early stage of the compliance process.

The manufacturer should also ensure that the product submitted for approval is technically identical to the equipment intended for commercial importation and distribution.

Changes to radio characteristics, technical specifications, hardware, or other regulated elements may affect the approval status and should be assessed before products are introduced into the market.

AFAQ JOOD Regulatory Support

AFAQ JOOD supports manufacturers, OEMs, ODMs, exporters, distributors, and technology companies with Type Approval and regulatory coordination across Middle East and African markets.

Our team can assist with regulatory assessment, technical documentation, manufacturer authorization, local applicant coordination, Type Approval applications, compliance documentation, and regulatory follow-up for telecommunications, RF, wireless, IoT, networking, and other regulated technology products entering the South African market.

whatKnow.en:
Manufacturers, importers, distributors, and technology companies supplying telecommunications and radio equipment to South Africa should ensure that their products comply with the applicable ICASA Type Approval requirements before importation, sale, or use.

International manufacturers should pay particular attention to the local applicant requirement, as ICASA Type Approval Certificates are issued to South African registered companies.

Depending on the equipment category, applicants may need to provide technical documentation, product specifications, user manuals, photographs, declarations of conformity, and applicable RF, EMC, safety, and performance test reports from recognized laboratories.

Manufacturers should also ensure that the equipment submitted for Type Approval is technically identical to the equipment intended for commercial importation and distribution in South Africa.

Changes to the product’s hardware, radio characteristics, technical specifications, or other regulated features may require regulatory assessment and could affect the existing Type Approval.

Companies should also verify the ICASA Type Approval Register before submitting a new application, as equipment that is identical to an already approved model may qualify for the applicable simplified procedure.
